Outcome: Depressive symptoms (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Older adults with vitamin D deficiency had much higher odds of depressive symptoms than those with sufficient vitamin D.
Sentence: "Ordinal logistic regression showed that vitamin D deficiency (OR = 19.7, 95% CI 5.60, 74.86, p < 0.001) and insufficiency (OR = 6.40, 95% CI 2.20, 19.91, p < 0.001) were associated with higher odds of having depressive symptoms."
Measured as: depressive symptoms (15-item GDS)
Population: Adults aged 65 years and older attending primary healthcare centers in Kuwait
Intervention: Serum 25-OH-D level (deficient <50 nmol/L, insufficient 50-75 nmol/L, sufficient >=75 nmol/L), measured not assigned
Comparator: Sufficient vitamin D group
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 237
baseline_vitamin_d_status: mixed

## Study B
Found: harm
Claim: In PD patients given vitamin D3, folic acid and B12 for 6 months, the 15D depression dimension score significantly increased (improved) from baseline.
Sentence: "After the intervention, the mean score of speech, mental function, discomfort and symptoms, depression, and QoL significantly increased (p < 0.05 for all)."
Measured as: depression (15D dimension score)
Population: Levodopa-treated Parkinson's disease patients in Romania, mean age 71 years
Intervention: Daily tablet with 800 IU vitamin D3, 1000 µg folic acid, 15 µg vitamin B12 for 6 months
Comparator: None (single-arm, baseline vs 6 months)
Design: case series
Sample size: not reported
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Responses

### Response A
```json
{
 "rationale": "A cross-sectional association in older adults with deficiency differs from a single-arm Parkinson's study of a vitamin D3/folic acid/B12 combination, with no comparator and a different design and depression measure.",
 "verdict": "genuine",
 "reason": "design_or_bias",
 "also_differs": [
  "population",
  "intervention",
  "comparator",

 ],

}
```
